title: Psalms Bible Quiz - Chapter 119
description: Ten questions on Psalms 119: the long psalm in praise of God's word, law and statutes - a lamp to the feet, sweeter than honey and better than gold.

questions.text: How can a young man keep his way pure, according to verse 9?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:9 answers: "By living according to your word."

answers.text: By serving in the temple courts each day
By living according to your word

questions.text: Why has the psalmist hidden God's word in his heart?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:11 says "I have hidden your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you."

answers.text: That he might not sin against God
That he might teach the young men of his people

questions.text: What have God's statutes been to the psalmist in the house where he lives?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:54 says "Your statutes have been my songs in the house where I live."

questions.text: At what time will the psalmist rise to give thanks because of God's righteous ordinances?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:62 says "At midnight I will rise to give thanks to you."

questions.text: What is the law of God's mouth better than, according to verse 72?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:72 says the law of your mouth is better than thousands of pieces of gold and silver.

answers.text: A house full of grain and new wine
The crown of a great king
Great flocks and herds of cattle
Thousands of pieces of gold and silver

questions.text: What does the psalmist say he has become like in verse 83?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:83 says "I have become like a wineskin in the smoke."

answers.text: A tree planted by the water

questions.text: How sweet are God's promises to the psalmist's taste?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:103 says "How sweet are your promises to my taste, more than honey to my mouth!"

answers.text: More than wine at a feast
More than honey to his mouth

questions.text: Complete verse 105: "Your word is a lamp to my ..."
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:105 says "Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path."

questions.text: How often a day does the psalmist praise God because of his righteous ordinances?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:164 says "Seven times a day, I praise you."

questions.text: In the last verse, what does the psalmist say he has gone astray like?
questions.explanation: Psalms 119:176 says "I have gone astray like a lost sheep. Seek your servant."
